DigitalOcean (NYSE: DOCN)Q4 2024 Earnings CallFeb 25, 2025, 8:00 a.m.
ET
...
Revenue growth accelerated in the fourth quarter to 13% year over year to 205 million with one of our biggest growth levers, net dollar retention improving to 99% from 96% in Q4 of the prior year.
...
On top of the encouraging growth signals, profitability remained strong as we delivered healthy 42% adjusted EBITDA margin, both Q4 and for the full year, maintaining our cost discipline while we continue to invest to fuel future growth.
Looking forward, our 2025 guidance reflects this ongoing momentum with full-year revenue growth at low to mid-teens and high teens free cash flow margins above our preliminary 15% to 17% indication.
...
Revenue in the fourth quarter was 205 million, up 13% year over year.
Annual run rate revenue, or ARR, in the fourth quarter was 820 million as we added 26 million of incremental ARR in the quarter, up from 24 million in new ARR in Q3.
Of note, we made a methodology change to how we report ARR, where we now calculate ARR by multiplying the quarterly revenue times four rather than the final month of the quarter times 12.
...
Revenue from our builders and scalers, which are our highest-spending customer cohorts and represent 88% of total revenue, grew 16% year over year, and customer count increased 6% year over year.
...
Gross margin for the quarter was 62%, which was 300 basis points higher than the prior quarter and 500 basis points higher than the prior year.
...
Q4 adjusted free cash flow was 37 million or 18% of revenue.
...
For 2024, total revenue increased 13% year over year to 781 million.
...
Moving on to guidance.
I will now share our financial outlook for the first quarter of 2025 and for the full year.
For the first quarter of 2025, we expect revenue to be in the range of 207 million to 209 million, representing approximately 13% year-over-year growth at the midpoint of our guidance range.
For the full year 2025, we expect revenue to be in the range of 870 million to 890 million, also representing approximately 13% at the midpoint of our range.
…
For the first quarter of 2025, we expect our adjusted EBITDA margins to be in the range of 38% to 40%.
For the full year, we expect adjusted EBITDA margins to be in the range of 37% to 40%.
For the first quarter of 2025, we expect non-GAAP diluted earnings per share to be $0.41 to $0.46 based on approximately 103 million to 104 million in weighted average fully diluted shares outstanding.
For the full year 2025, we expect non-GAAP diluted earnings per share to be $1.85 to $1.95 based on approximately 104 million to 105 million in weighted average fully diluted shares outstanding.
On adjusted free cash flow, we expect adjusted free cash flow margins for the full year to be in the range of 16% to 18%, slightly ahead of the preliminary indication for 2025 that we provided last quarter.
...
And we remain very confident in our ability to deliver the 16% to 18% full-year adjusted free cash flow margin in our guide.

{"figures":[{"fact_key":"Start date","value":"2023-09-01"},{"fact_key":"End date","value":"2026-09-09"},{"fact_key":"Purchases and sales","value":1},{"fact_key":"Starting capital","value":1000},{"fact_key":"Total money contributed","value":1000},{"fact_key":"Ending portfolio value","value":4963},{"fact_key":"Total return on starting capital","value":396.3},{"fact_key":"Benchmark return","value":69},{"fact_key":"Return difference versus benchmark","value":327.3},{"fact_key":"Worst drop from a prior high","value":44.9},{"fact_key":"Worst drop began","value":"2025-02-18"},{"fact_key":"Worst drop ended","value":"2025-08-01"},{"fact_key":"Portfolio value before the worst drop","value":1747},{"fact_key":"Portfolio value at the bottom of the worst drop","value":963}],"language":"es-419","text":"Entre el 1 de septiembre de 2023 y el 9 de septiembre de 2026, la experiencia fue comprar DOCN una vez y mantenerlo, sin aportar más dinero. Los $1,000 iniciales terminaron en $4,963, un rendimiento total de 396.3%. En otras palabras, el crecimiento vino de la inversión, no de depósitos adicionales.

El resultado estuvo relacionado con una historia de expansión en el negocio de DigitalOcean. La empresa reportó que sus ingresos de 2024 crecieron 13% y que el crecimiento de clientes de mayor gasto se aceleró, aunque su guía para 2025 apuntaba a un crecimiento más moderado, de alrededor de 13% ([resultados del cuarto trimestre de 2024](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024-Financial-Results/default.aspx)). Más adelante, DigitalOcean informó que sus ingresos del segundo trimestre de 2025 crecieron 14% y elevó su guía anual, señales que ayudan a explicar la recuperación posterior ([resultados del segundo trimestre de 2025](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx)). Eso ofrece contexto para el avance, pero no demuestra que un evento específico haya causado cada movimiento del precio.

Mantener no fue un recorrido tranquilo. Desde un máximo previo, el portafolio cayó 44.9% entre el 18 de febrero y el 1 de agosto de 2025: pasó de $1,747 a $963. Ese descenso llevó el saldo temporalmente por debajo de los $1,000 iniciales. Después, el valor se recuperó y terminó bastante por encima de ese punto bajo, aunque por debajo de su máximo registrado.

Frente al benchmark SPY, la diferencia fue muy amplia. SPY obtuvo 69.0% en el mismo periodo, mientras DOCN obtuvo 396.3%, una ventaja de 327.3 puntos porcentuales. El benchmark representa una canasta amplia de grandes empresas estadounidenses, mientras que esta prueba concentró todo en una sola compañía, por lo que el resultado superior vino acompañado de una experiencia mucho más dependiente de los acontecimientos de DOCN. El contexto general también fue favorable para las acciones estadounidenses durante buena parte del periodo, con avances del S&P 500 en 2024 y 2025 ([datos históricos del S&P 500](https://ycharts.com/indices/%5ESPX)), pero eso por sí solo no explica la magnitud de la diferencia."}
